acceptance: Red first: tierArgs (or the IntegrationTier argv seen by an injected runner) carries a -timeout derived from TierAttempt; red on main, where no -timeout is passed
A package that runs longer than 10 minutes but inside TierAttempt is not killed by the go test default (test with an injected runner and a fake clock or a recorded argv, never a real 10 minute run)
A run that exceeds TierAttempt still ends as a deadline hit with the existing typed outcome
100% coverage on each changed function, zero code comments, and the ciparitygate package note in STE
fix: Derive the go test -timeout from the one home of the budget: the TierAttempt context deadline less a small margin, passed by tierArgs, so the context, not the go test default, bounds the run and a real timeout is reported as a deadline hit. Apply the same rule to the serialized retake. Red test first.
summary: Cycle 2576 (wave 184) FAILED as a false rejection after 264 LLM minutes. tierArgs in go/internal/phases/audit/ciparitygate/tier.go builds go test -race -count=1 -p N -parallel N -tags integration <pkgs> with no -timeout. Go then applies its default 10 minute per-package timeout and panics in ./cmd/evolve, which needs about 760-800 s under -race on a loaded host, before the gate's own budget g.timeouts.TierAttempt (15 minutes) ends. The serialized retake times out the same way, so the audit reports a red that the change did not cause.
title: The audit integration tier runs go test with no -timeout, so the 10 minute default kills cmd/evolve before the tier's own 15 minute budget
